summary: Explains the Chaos Cloth Panel node editor workflow: a standalone cloth asset built from DCC-exported static meshes via a Dataflow graph, then attached to any skeletal or static mesh with a Chaos Cloth Component; compares it with the legacy cloth editor.
gotchas: Slightly higher rendering cost than legacy cloth because the cloth asset is rendered by a separate component (more draw calls)
Needs separate render and simulation meshes exported as FBX static meshes

summary: Part 1 of the C++ first-person adventure tutorial: create a Blueprint First Person (Arena Shooter) project, add a C++ AGameModeBase subclass via Tools > New C++ Class, build in Visual Studio, derive a BP_ Game Mode, set it as Default GameMode, and print an on-screen debug message from StartPlay().
gotchas: Recommends disabling Live Coding on a new project; it can error when editing headers or compiling from Visual Studio
C++ classes only appear in the Content Browser after building from VS at least once (restart editor if not)
Always choose Public class type so headers go in the module's Public folder
Sample levels need GameMode Override changed in World Settings

summary: Part 2 of the C++ first-person tutorial: create an ACharacter C++ subclass and BP child, set it as Default Pawn Class, and explore the template's Input Actions (IA_Jump, IA_Move, IA_Look) and Input Mapping Contexts, including Negate, Swizzle Input Axis Values, Dead Zone and Scalar modifiers, then merge mappings into IMC_Adventure.
gotchas: New character can't move or look until body, camera and actions are added in later parts

summary: Part 3 of the C++ first-person tutorial: add EnhancedInput to Build.cs, declare UInputMappingContext/UInputAction TObjectPtr properties, implement Move() with AddMovementInput, bind Move/Jump/StopJumping via UEnhancedInputComponent::BindAction in SetupPlayerInputComponent, and add the mapping context through UEnhancedInputLocalPlayerSubsystem in BeginPlay.
gotchas: #include statements must come before the .generated.h include
Remove the Super::SetupPlayerInputComponent call and cast to UEnhancedInputComponent instead
Assign IMC/IA assets in the Character Blueprint's Input category or input won't work

summary: Part 4 of the C++ first-person tutorial: implement Look() with AddControllerYawInput/PitchInput, create a UCameraComponent and first-person USkeletalMeshComponent with CreateDefaultSubobject, attach the camera to the head socket, configure First Person Rendering (FirstPersonPrimitiveType, first-person FOV/scale), owner-only visibility and shadows, and assign an Animation Blueprint via SetAnimInstanceClass.
gotchas: FirstPerson-type primitives render in a separate pass and don't cast world shadows; cast shadow from the hidden third-person mesh
Visibility/shadow setup works more reliably in BeginPlay than in the constructor
Data-only Blueprint must be opened with Open Full Blueprint Editor to see components
Set mesh rotation Z -90 and location Z -95 in the editor to fit the capsule

summary: Part 5 of the C++ first-person tutorial on data-driven items: define an FItemData struct deriving from FTableRowBase with UENUM/USTRUCT types, a UDataAsset subclass (UItemDefinition) holding a soft-referenced world mesh, then create a Data Asset instance and a Data Table using that row struct.
gotchas: Data Tables can't store hard UObject references; use TSoftObjectPtr
Put shared headers under the module's Public folder so other code can include them
Make Row Name match the Data Asset's ID for easier lookups

summary: Part 6 of the C++ first-person tutorial: build an APickupBase actor that loads a Data Table row with FindRow and LoadSynchronous, sets its static mesh, uses a query-only USphereComponent overlapping only Pawn, binds OnComponentBeginOverlap with AddDynamic, respawns via FTimerManager::SetTimer, and refreshes in-editor with PostEditChangeProperty.
gotchas: Call RemoveAll(this) on the delegate before AddDynamic so the overlap binds only once across reloads
Set a root component explicitly in C++ or the engine may pick a different one on recompile
Pickup Item ID must exactly match the Data Table row ID or initialization fails
PostEditChangeProperty must be wrapped in #if WITH_EDITOR

summary: Part 7 of the C++ first-person tutorial: add a virtual CreateItemCopy (DuplicateObject, GetTransientPackage), an EquippableToolDefinition data asset and AEquippableToolBase actor, a UInventoryComponent, and character AttachTool/GiveItem logic that spawns the tool, attaches it to the HandGrip_R socket, swaps Anim Blueprints and adds a priority-1 tool mapping context; builds a Dart Launcher with IA_UseTool and IMC_DartLauncher.
gotchas: Use Cast<> rather than CastChecked<> for tool input binding so a failed cast doesn't crash
Tool mapping context priority 1 overrides the base context (priority 0) on shared keys
Set the tool mesh's First Person Primitive Type to First Person to join the first-person render pass
Duplicated ABP_FP_Pistol must be re-pointed from BP_FPShooter to your character Blueprint

summary: Final part of the C++ first-person tutorial: create an AFirstPersonProjectile with USphereComponent, UProjectileMovementComponent and OnComponentHit impulse logic, a camera line trace (LineTraceSingleByChannel, ECC_Visibility) for aim, and spawn projectiles from the pistol's Muzzle socket using FindLookAtRotation and FActorSpawnParameters.
gotchas: ProjectileMovement assumes +X is forward; rotate the dart mesh to match
Up to 18 custom collision profiles under Project Settings > Engine > Collision
If firing does nothing, check IA_UseTool is assigned to Use Action on the character Blueprint

summary: Explains how Object Types and Block/Overlap/Ignore responses combine between two bodies, when hit and overlap events fire (Simulation Generates Hit Events, Generate Overlap Events), with worked sphere-vs-wall examples.
gotchas: Both bodies must Block each other's object types to collide
Overlap events require Generate Overlap Events on both actors
Hit-reporting objects spam events while resting on something; filter them
Simulate in Editor camera is not a pawn and generates no collision

summary: Reference table for the Collision Presets section of a BodyInstance: built-in presets (BlockAll, OverlapAllDynamic, Pawn, Trigger, etc.), Collision Enabled states, default Object Types, Ignore/Overlap/Block meanings, and the Visibility/Camera trace responses.
gotchas: No Collision bodies can't be used for raycasts, sweeps or overlaps
Query Only can't simulate; Physics Only can't be queried

summary: Hub page for collision geometry setup tutorials; contains no content of its own in this extract.

Explains simple (primitive/convex) versus complex (trimesh) collision and the Static Mesh Editor Collision Complexity options: Project Default, Simple And Complex, Use Simple Collision As Complex, Use Complex Collision As Simple.
gotchas: Objects using UseComplexAsSimple cannot simulate physics, though they can collide with simulated simple objects

summary: How-to for generating convex-hull collision on a static mesh with the Static Mesh Editor's Collision > Auto Convex Collision tool (V-HACD), with example Hull Count, Max Hull Verts and Hull Precision values.
gotchas: Computation runs as a background task in the Static Mesh Editor

summary: Shows how to add custom object and trace channels and custom collision presets in Project Settings > Collision.
gotchas: Limit of 18 custom object or trace channels

summary: Steps to add a custom Trace Response channel beyond Visibility and Camera in Project Settings > Engine > Collision, choosing its Default Response.
gotchas: Open Blueprint Editors must be closed and reopened to see the new channel
Actors must be set to block the new channel for traces to hit them

summary: Describes the Static Mesh Editor Collision menu's K-DOP generators (10, 18, 26 DOP) that fit bevelled box hulls to a mesh, suited to pipes, pillars and railings.
Short how-to on adding basic primitive collision shapes in the Static Mesh Editor and the keyboard controls for moving, deleting, focusing and duplicating physics bodies.
Lists in-game console commands for inspecting collision: show COLLISION to draw collision and blocking volumes, and stat game for collision timing stats.

Setup tutorial for the navigation areas/query filters quick start: create a Third Person Blueprint project, a level with a NavMeshBoundsVolume, and an NPC Blueprint that calls AI Move to Actor with an instance-editable Filter Class variable.

Quick start for steering AI paths by cost: create Nav Area Blueprint classes (Default Cost, Fixed Area Entering Cost, Draw Color) applied via Nav Modifier Volumes, and Navigation Query Filter Blueprints with Travel Cost Override assigned to Move to Actor's Filter Class.
gotchas: Requires the setup from the Preparation Guide page

summary: Explains the Data Registry plugin: global USTRUCT data storage with ordered Data Registry Sources and Meta Data Registry Sources (wrapping Data Tables and Curve Tables), FDataRegistryType/FDataRegistryId identifiers, and the UDataRegistrySubsystem/UDataRegistry lookup functions including async AcquireItem.
gotchas: Registry Type names must be unique; duplicates mean only one registry is populated
With duplicate item IDs only the first loaded item is retrievable
Caching struct pointers from a registry is unsafe as items can unload
For per-session state like story progress use Save Game instead

summary: Step-by-step setup for Data Registries: enable the Data Registry plugin, set Directories to Scan in Project Settings > Game > Data Registry, create a Data Registry asset with Registry Type, Item Struct and Data Sources, preview with Refresh, and add DataRegistry to Build.cs for C++.
gotchas: Restart the editor after enabling the plugin before the settings category appears
Feature still in development; some Cache settings might not work as expected
Only the first-discovered instance of a duplicated row is accessible

summary: Conceptual overview of the Dataflow Graph: a dependency-based, non-destructive node graph asset for procedurally generating physics assets such as Chaos Cloth, Chaos Flesh and Geometry Collection fracturing, extensible with C++ nodes.
